1

What data exists

Every labelled example in this project is a one-second window: the court positions of six players and the ball, sampled at 30 fps for 29 frames. Three corpus generations exist because the detector was corrected twice and source videos were added over time — so each figure below names the corpus it was computed on.

2

Detection & tracking

Before a tactic can be classified, the pipeline has to find six players and a fast, tiny ball in an uncalibrated broadcast frame that also contains the other team, coaches, referees and crowd. These figures quantify how well that works.

3

Tactics & biomechanics

These figures translate the tracked coordinates into the vocabulary a coach or sports scientist uses — approach speed, spacing, synchrony, role kinematics — and show what the deployed model actually produces for a match.

4

Model comparison

Nine classical models and a rule engine were scored under two protocols: stratified k-fold (clips from one video on both sides) and leave-one-video-out (every clip of the held-out video unseen). The gap between them is the headline result of the project.

5

Deep temporal models

Five sequence architectures — Mamba (SSM), Transformer, TCN, BiLSTM and InceptionTime — were trained on the identical (29, 18) tensor under one shared hyper-parameter budget, then held to a pre-registered bar against the deployed gradient-boosting model.

Volleyball Tactical Data Atlas  ·  generated from finalyearproject/figures_atlas  ·  regenerate with python make_data_atlas.py

Corpus versions are not interchangeable: v1 (285 clips, pre-detector-fix), v3 (375, fixed pipeline, 3 videos), v4 (945, 6+ videos). Every figure names the corpus it was computed on. Leave-one-video-out is the honest cross-video number throughout; k-fold is reported only to measure the gap.
